pages.title: History
pages.content:
Sixty-four years,
one decision at a time.

(Since 1962) one decision at a time.

196219781987199420032009201620212026

Ishizue Holdings B.V. began in Rotterdam in 1962, when Kenzo Ishizue and Anneke de Vries started a stone and aggregates trade on the Maas. The record since then is nine dated decisions, from the first yard to the interim report of 2026.

1962

(Since 1962)

Stone and aggregates on the Maas

In 1962 Kenzo Ishizue and Anneke de Vries started a stone and aggregates trade on the Maas in Rotterdam. The name they chose, ishizue, means foundation stone. That trade continues as Ishizue Materials, based in Rotterdam, with 640 people working in stone, aggregates and recycled building materials. It is the first of the six companies. The founders owned the business themselves in those early years. The holding company, the Ishizue Foundation and the employee share plan all came later, in 2003. What 1962 fixed was the trade, the city and the habit of staying with a business once it had been taken on. The group still dates itself from that year, and from the quay where the materials moved.

Ishizue Materials

Rotterdam, NL · 640 people

1978

(Two trucks and a depot)

Northquay joins

Northquay Logistics joined in 1978 and is based in Antwerp. The company's own story of those early years opens with two trucks and a depot. The work today is warehousing and regional freight, and 920 people do it, more colleagues than any other company in the group. The name on the door stayed Northquay. Local managers still run the warehouses and the routes. Antwerp gave the Rotterdam materials yard a sister company in another harbour city, with its own trade and its own people. Patient ownership and local management, phrases the group still uses, were already the shape of this second decision. Northquay remains a Belgian freight business inside a Dutch-registered holding company.

Northquay Logistics

Antwerp, BE · 920 people

1987

(Maaskade 41)

The head office moves

In 1987 the head office moved to Maaskade 41, 3071 NE Rotterdam, and it has stayed there. Fifty-eight people of Ishizue Holdings B.V. work in the building, within a group of 2,860 colleagues. The address is a low rise of pale stone and glass on the harbour quay, the place the group asks guests, owners and readers of the accounts to use. Reception is open Monday to Friday, from 08:30 to 17:30 CET, and visits are by appointment on Tuesday and Thursday. The telephone is +31 10 555 0141. From 2003 this was also the address of a formally constituted holding company, with the Ishizue Foundation as majority owner. Reports are published from here, voluntarily, because the group is privately held.

1994

(Keep the name)

Lindholm joins

Lindholm Precision joined in 1994. The company is based in Gothenburg and employs 310 people who machine metal components. The ordinary picture of the work is a technician measuring a part with calipers beside a CNC machine. The succession that brought Lindholm into the group left the name on the door, left management local and left the sites in Gothenburg. That is the same outcome the group still describes for the first 100 days after a closing: the name, the management and the sites stay. Lindholm is the workshop the group can point to when an owner asks what keeping the name means after the papers are signed. The trade stayed machined components, and it stayed in Sweden.

Lindholm Precision

Gothenburg, SE · 310 people

2003

(Foundation majority)

A holding company, and a share plan

In 2003 the business became Ishizue Holdings B.V. The Ishizue Foundation took the majority of the shares. An employee share plan started in the same year, so colleagues could hold a stake beside the Foundation. The group is privately held. It publishes its reports because it chooses to. The annual report appears every March, and a sustainability statement is published with it. The shape set in 2003 is the shape in use now: a foundation as majority owner, an employee plan, operating companies under their own names, and a holding office of 58 people at Maaskade 41. The revised corporate governance code adopted on 15 January 2026 is the current code of that privately held group. An independent chair leads the board.

2009

(Building services)

Verda joins

Verda Facilities joined in 2009. The base is Utrecht, in the Netherlands, and 552 people work in building services and maintenance. The daily work is plant rooms, ventilation and the fabric of buildings other people occupy. Verda also trains 40 technicians a year, apprentices learning the trade at the bench with an instructor. The group repeats that figure as a yearly intake, the number trained each year inside a company that already employs 552. The name stayed Verda. The base stayed Utrecht. Local management stayed with the people who know the sites. Verda was the fourth company to join, after materials, freight and precision machining, and it remains a Dutch building-services business with its own door.

Verda Facilities

Utrecht, NL · 552 people

2016

(Food ingredients)

Calder joins

Calder Food Partners joined in 2016. The base is Hamburg, in Germany, and 260 people distribute food ingredients. The work has a laboratory side: people sampling grains and seeds before those ingredients move on to someone else's product. The sector line the group publishes is food ingredient distribution, and Calder has kept that line, its name and its Hamburg management. It was the fifth company, after Ishizue Materials, Northquay Logistics, Lindholm Precision and Verda Facilities. Joining took the group into food while the other companies kept the trades they already had. Calder's colleagues sit inside the count of 2,860 people across nine countries. The name on the door in Hamburg is still Calder Food Partners.

Calder Food Partners

Hamburg, DE · 260 people

2021

(Forty rooftops)

Renewables joins

Ishizue Renewables joined in 2021. The base is Aarhus, in Denmark, and 120 people work in rooftop solar and storage for industrial sites. A notice on 1 July 2026 recorded the company's 40th rooftop site. Capacity across those sites is 38 MW. The story the group tells of that moment is titled "Forty rooftops: Ishizue Renewables at five", marking five years inside the group. Engineers walk flat warehouse roofs; the panels and the storage are the plant. Renewables is the sixth company to join, and the latest. The name carries Ishizue. Northquay, Lindholm, Verda and Calder kept the names they brought. The sector sits beside the others: stone, freight, machining, building services, food ingredients and power on roofs the customers already use.

Ishizue Renewables

Aarhus, DK · 120 people

2026

(A voluntary report)

The first half of 2026

On 28 August 2026 Ishizue Holdings B.V. published its interim report for the first half of 2026. The same year had already brought the annual report for 2025 and the sustainability statement, on 27 March; the annual general meeting on 21 May, at which all resolutions were adopted; the Renewables rooftop notice on 1 July; and, on 15 January, the adoption of a revised corporate governance code. The next date is the third-quarter trading update on 12 November 2026. The year is the present on the group's timeline. The count is still six companies, 2,860 colleagues and nine countries, reporting from Maaskade 41 because the board publishes voluntarily. The annual report for 2026 is due on 26 March 2027, and the following annual general meeting on 20 May 2027.

Group companies

pages.title: Group companies
pages.content:
Six companies,
one owner.

(Six companies) one owner.

Six companies sit under one owner, Ishizue Holdings B.V., joined between 1962 and 2021. Each line below keeps the same four facts: the year, the base, the people and the sector.

(Six companies) One owner

Ishizue Holdings B.V. owns six operating companies and employs 2,860 colleagues in nine countries: the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Denmark, Sweden, Poland, France, Spain and Ireland. The holding office at Maaskade 41 accounts for 58 of those people. The companies joined in the order of their years, from the founders' stone trade in 1962 to rooftop solar in 2021. Majority ownership sits with the Ishizue Foundation. An employee share plan has run since 2003, the year the holding company was formed. The group is privately held and publishes its reports voluntarily, with the annual report every March. Currency in the accounts is the euro. What the owner in Rotterdam asks of a company is narrow and repeated: keep the name, keep local management, reinvest in the trade first, and take one long view. People come before a tidy structure.

01 — 1962

(Stone and aggregates) since 1962.

Ishizue Materials

Ishizue Materials is the company Kenzo Ishizue and Anneke de Vries began on the Maas. The word ishizue means foundation stone, and it is still the name on this door and on the holding company. Recycled building materials sit in the same sector line as the original stone and aggregates trade. Local management runs the yard. The company is the first of the six, which is why the group still describes later joiners as businesses that keep their own names. Of the 2,860 colleagues, 640 are here, in the city where the head office has stood at Maaskade 41 since 1987. The trade and the holding office share Rotterdam and remain distinct.

The name stayed Northquay when the company joined. Managers in Antwerp run the depots and the routes. The holding office in Rotterdam is 58 people and is built to leave that local management in place. Northquay is the second company, sixteen years of group history after the materials yard and well before the holding company was formed in 2003. The name, the Gothenburg sites and the local management all stayed through the change of owner. That outcome matches the rule the group still states for a new company: through the first 100 days, the name, the management and the sites are kept. The name stayed Verda, and the base stayed Utrecht, a second Dutch company beside Ishizue Materials in Rotterdam and beside the holding office. Local managers run the contracts. Calder was the fifth company, and it brought food into a group that already held materials, freight, machining and building services, while those four kept their own trades. Two hundred and sixty people are Calder's share of the 2,860. The company sits in Germany, one of the nine countries where colleagues work, with its own base and its own name.

Ishizue Renewables

The panels stand on warehouse roofs the customers already use, and storage is part of the same sector line. The name carries Ishizue. One hundred and twenty people run the work from Aarhus, the smallest of the six companies by headcount and the latest to join. The story "Forty rooftops: Ishizue Renewables at five" marks five years in the group. Local management remains in Denmark. The March sustainability statement is where the year's account of these sites is published with the annual report.

The name and the managers stay

A company that joins keeps the name on the door and keeps the managers who know the work. Northquay Logistics, Lindholm Precision, Verda Facilities and Calder Food Partners brought names that are still the names in use. Ishizue Materials carries the founders' word, and Ishizue Renewables carries it as well. Local management is the ordinary arrangement at each base: Rotterdam, Antwerp, Gothenburg, Utrecht, Hamburg and Aarhus. The holding office at Maaskade 41 is 58 people within the 2,860, sized to own for the long term and to leave the trades where they are. Reinvesting in the company comes before a new structure. The Ishizue Foundation holds the majority. Colleagues take part through the employee share plan begun in 2003. Reports on the whole of this are published voluntarily.

pages.title: Leadership
pages.content:
The people who
answer for the group.

(Six people) answer for the group.

Six people answer for Ishizue Holdings B.V. from the head office at Maaskade 41. Kenzo Ishizue and Anneke de Vries, who founded the trade in 1962, are recorded with them as the start of the line.

(Independent chair)

Grace Abernethy

Chair of the Board (independent)

Grace Abernethy is Chair of the Board, and she is independent. The board she chairs has seven members, four of them independent. Her remit is the long-term ownership of Ishizue Holdings B.V.: that the Ishizue Foundation's majority and the employee share plan, in place since 2003, stay in view, and that the six companies are owned on a long clock. The annual report, published every March, is part of what the chair answers for, together with the sustainability statement published beside it. The revised corporate governance code adopted on 15 January 2026 is the current code. She chairs the holding company's board at Maaskade 41. Operating management stays with the companies: materials, freight, machining, building services, food ingredients and rooftop solar. The separation between an independent chair and a group chief executive is deliberate.

(The six companies)

Daniel Okoro

Group CEO

Daniel Okoro is Group CEO. He answers for the six companies as one group: Ishizue Materials in Rotterdam, Northquay Logistics in Antwerp, Lindholm Precision in Gothenburg, Verda Facilities in Utrecht, Calder Food Partners in Hamburg and Ishizue Renewables in Aarhus. Together they are 2,860 colleagues in nine countries, a figure that includes the 58 people at the holding office on Maaskade 41. The chief executive's remit is the long view the group states in public. Companies keep their names and their local managers. The holding office stays small beside the operating companies, which is what "people before structure" means in practice. The latest account published under this leadership is the interim report for the first half of 2026, issued on 28 August 2026. The group has been privately held, and reporting voluntarily, throughout his tenure as the public face of management.

(Treasury and reporting)

Sofia Marchetti

CFO · investor contact

Sofia Marchetti is CFO, and she is the contact for investors. Mail about reports and the calendar goes to ir@ishizue-holdings.example, and that mailbox replies within two business days. Her remit is treasury and reporting: the interim report, the annual report each March, the sustainability statement published with it, and the trading updates on the financial calendar. The next of those is the third-quarter update on 12 November 2026, then the annual report for 2026 on 26 March 2027, then the annual general meeting on 20 May 2027. The group is privately held. The Ishizue Foundation owns the majority, so the figures she presents are the ones the board has chosen to publish. She starts from a stable public line: six companies, 2,860 colleagues, nine countries, founded in 1962. Press mail is a separate box, press@ishizue-holdings.example, with the same two-day reply.

(Continuity for owners)

Arjun Mehta

Head of Investments

Arjun Mehta is Head of Investments. Owners of businesses write to him when they want a conversation about passing a company on. The first conversation is free and confidential. A business review takes about six weeks. There is one written offer. Signing and closing typically take ten to fourteen weeks from that first conversation. In the first 100 days the name, the management and the sites stay. He looks at companies that have been profitable for at least five years, with revenue from €10 million to €80 million, and with 50 to 600 employees, in Northern or Western Europe. The owner wants continuity. A succession review for a company that wants the thinking on its own is a separate shared service, €3,500 one-off, and the first meeting of that review is free. His name is the one on the page for owners.

(Counsel and the board record)

Elin Halvorsen

General Counsel and Company Secretary

Elin Halvorsen is General Counsel and Company Secretary. She keeps the board's record and the corporate governance code, including the revised code adopted on 15 January 2026. The board has seven members, four of them independent, with Grace Abernethy as independent chair. Three committees sit under that board: Audit, Remuneration and Nomination, and Sustainability. Colleagues can use an independent speak-up channel, and a report made there receives a reply within five business days. Company secretarial work covers the annual general meeting, including the meeting of 21 May 2026 at which all resolutions were adopted, and the meeting set for 20 May 2027. Her office is at Maaskade 41 with the rest of the holding company. The code and the minutes are how a privately held group, publishing voluntarily, keeps a record someone outside the room can later read.

(Published fees)

Tomasz Wrona

Head of Shared Services

Tomasz Wrona is Head of Shared Services. The back office he runs serves the group and is offered to independent companies of 20 to 300 people. Fees are published in euros, exclusive of VAT at 21 percent, and the published list is the tariff. Payroll and HR administration, covering payslips, filings, leave records and one named contact, is €38 per employee per month. The first call is free. Notice is 30 days. There is no minimum term beyond three months. The other lines, from bookkeeping to the owner succession review, are set out in full on the shared-services page, including the free first meeting of that review. He is the named contact for a company that wants to start. Publishing the fee, and naming a person beside it, is the group's answer to a back office that other people can use.

(The founders, 1962)

Kenzo Ishizue and Anneke de Vries

Co-founders, 1962

Kenzo Ishizue and Anneke de Vries founded the business in 1962 in Rotterdam, as traders in stone and aggregates on the Maas. They are named in the history of the group. The word they chose, ishizue, means foundation stone, and it remains the name of the holding company and of two operating companies, Ishizue Materials and Ishizue Renewables. The other four companies kept the names they had when they joined. From 2003 the majority owner has been the Ishizue Foundation, and colleagues have taken part through the employee share plan begun that year. The decision the group still quotes from the founders is a plain one: lay a foundation that later companies can be built on, and keep each trade recognisable to the people who run it. Sixty-four years on, the head office they would recognise by address has been Maaskade 41 since 1987.

Governance

pages.title: Governance
pages.content:
Owned for the
long term.

(Foundation majority) since 2003.

The Ishizue Foundation owns the majority of Ishizue Holdings B.V., and colleagues have taken part through an employee share plan since 2003. The board publishes its annual report every March.

Who owns the shares

Ishizue Holdings B.V. is privately held. The Ishizue Foundation owns the majority of the shares. An employee share plan has given colleagues a stake beside that majority since 2003, the year the holding company was formed. The operating companies sit under that owner and keep their own names and local management. The holding office at Maaskade 41 is 58 people, inside a group of 2,860 colleagues in nine countries and six companies. Because the shares are private, the group publishes reports by choice. The annual report appears every March, with the sustainability statement. An interim report for the first half of 2026 was published on 28 August 2026. Readers who want the primary documents use those reports. The ownership facts on this page are the ones the group states in every language: Foundation majority, employee plan since 2003, voluntary reporting.

Three principles

(Independent chair)

Grace Abernethy is Chair of the Board, and she is independent. The chair is a different seat from the Group CEO, Daniel Okoro, so the person who leads the board is not the person who leads day-to-day management of the six companies. Independence of the chair is one of the lines the group prints in its own governance summary, beside the shape of the board and the March report. The revised corporate governance code, adopted on 15 January 2026, is the current code. The annual general meeting on 21 May 2026 adopted all resolutions put to it. The next annual general meeting is set for 20 May 2027. Elin Halvorsen, General Counsel and Company Secretary, keeps the record of that board. The chair's work is done at Maaskade 41, for the holding company, while local managers stay in the companies.

(Seven board members, four independent)

The board has seven members. Four of the seven are independent, Grace Abernethy among them as chair. The group states that composition as a principle and holds to it. This page names the chair's independence and the count. It names the executives who answer publicly for their remits: Daniel Okoro as Group CEO, Sofia Marchetti as CFO, Arjun Mehta as Head of Investments, Elin Halvorsen as General Counsel and Company Secretary, and Tomasz Wrona as Head of Shared Services. Appointment years of individual directors are part of the board's own record. The public rule, repeated here so it can be checked, is seven members and four independent, with an independent chair. Committees of that board are Audit, Remuneration and Nomination, and Sustainability. The annual report each March is the narrative that sits beside this headcount.

(Annual report published every March)

The annual report is published every March, and the sustainability statement is published with it. On 27 March 2026 the group issued the annual report for 2025 and the sustainability statement. On 28 August 2026 it issued the interim report for the first half of 2026. The financial calendar that follows is short and dated: a third-quarter trading update on 12 November 2026, the annual report for 2026 on 26 March 2027, and the annual general meeting on 20 May 2027. Sofia Marchetti, the CFO, is the investor contact for these documents, at ir@ishizue-holdings.example, with a reply within two business days. Publication is voluntary. The group is privately held, the Ishizue Foundation holds the majority, and there is no listed quote beside the report. The March habit is the governance promise a reader can test by looking for the document.

Three committees

Three committees of the board sit in their own right: Audit, Remuneration and Nomination, and Sustainability. The committees are how a holding office of 58 people at Maaskade 41 separates those subjects. The people who answer for the group in public remain the chair and the five colleagues named beside her on the leadership page. Committee papers feed the report a reader can open.

(Audit)

Audit sits with the reports, the interim report and the annual report each March, and with the decision to keep publishing while the shares stay in private hands.

(Remuneration and Nomination)

Remuneration and Nomination sits with the board itself, a body of seven members, four of them independent, chaired independently by Grace Abernethy.

(Sustainability)

Sustainability sits with the statement published every March, with the work of Ishizue Renewables, with training at Verda Facilities, and with recycled building materials at Ishizue Materials.

The board at a glance

The code of conduct, and speaking up

The group keeps a code of conduct and a speak-up channel that is independent of line management. A person who uses that channel receives a reply within five business days. Elin Halvorsen, General Counsel and Company Secretary, is responsible for the code and for the board record around it. The revised corporate governance code adopted on 15 January 2026 is the current code. The channel is for concerns that should be heard outside the ordinary management line, and the five-day reply is the standard the group publishes, in the same spirit as the two business days it gives the investor and press mailboxes. Details of a report stay with the independent channel. The existence of the channel, the independence of it, and the reply time are the facts this page is able to state. The head office address for formal correspondence remains Maaskade 41, 3071 NE Rotterdam.

Investors

pages.title: Investors
pages.content:
Reports, notices
and dates.

(Reports) published by choice.

Reports and notices of Ishizue Holdings B.V. are published voluntarily for a privately held group. Sofia Marchetti, the CFO, answers investor mail within two business days.

6 companies · 2,860 colleagues · 9 countries · founded 1962

Six companies. 2,860 colleagues. Nine countries. Founded in 1962. Those are the key figures Ishizue Holdings B.V. states, in plain text, with no dashboard beside them. The six companies are Ishizue Materials, Northquay Logistics, Lindholm Precision, Verda Facilities, Calder Food Partners and Ishizue Renewables. The nine countries are the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Denmark, Sweden, Poland, France, Spain and Ireland. The holding office at Maaskade 41, Rotterdam, accounts for 58 of the 2,860. The Ishizue Foundation owns the majority. An employee share plan has run since 2003. The group is privately held and publishes reports voluntarily. Currency is the euro. The annual report appears every March, with the sustainability statement. Anyone looking for a traded share price will find the reports instead. Sofia Marchetti, the CFO, presents that published record and answers mail about it.

Financial calendar

The financial calendar is three dates. On 12 November 2026 the group publishes its third-quarter trading update. On 26 March 2027 it publishes the annual report for 2026. On 20 May 2027 it holds the annual general meeting. Those dates follow a year that already has its own record: the revised corporate governance code on 15 January 2026, the annual report for 2025 and the sustainability statement on 27 March 2026, the annual general meeting on 21 May 2026 at which all resolutions were adopted, the 40th rooftop notice on 1 July 2026, and the interim report for the first half of 2026 on 28 August 2026. The March report is the standing habit. The May meeting is the standing meeting. Interim and quarterly items are published as dated notices, and the calendar is updated when the board has set the day.

Reports

Two report publications anchor the current year. The annual report for 2025, together with the sustainability statement, was published on 27 March 2026. The interim report for the first half of 2026 was published on 28 August 2026. Both are reports of Ishizue Holdings B.V., issued from Maaskade 41, and both are available as documents from this page. The sustainability statement travels with the annual report each March. The next annual report, covering 2026, is scheduled for 26 March 2027. The group is privately held, so these documents are the account, published voluntarily, with the Ishizue Foundation as majority owner and the employee share plan in place since 2003. Format follows the document the board issues for that date. Questions about a report go to the investor mailbox, which replies within two business days.

Writing to the CFO

Investor relations

Sofia Marchetti

CFO · replies within two business days

ir@ishizue-holdings.example

Sofia Marchetti, CFO, is the investor contact. Write to ir@ishizue-holdings.example. The investor mailbox replies within two business days, as does the press mailbox at press@ishizue-holdings.example. General correspondence can go to contact@ishizue-holdings.example or by post to Ishizue Holdings B.V., Maaskade 41, 3071 NE Rotterdam, the Netherlands, or by telephone to +31 10 555 0141 during reception hours, Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 17:30 CET. She is the person named for treasury and reporting, including the calendar above. Visits to the office are by appointment on Tuesday and Thursday. A question about an owner bringing a company into the group goes to Arjun Mehta, Head of Investments. A question about buying the published back-office services goes to Tomasz Wrona. The investor line itself stays with the CFO and with the documents the board has published.

Sustainability

pages.title: Sustainability
pages.content:
Building on
what lasts.

(Three targets) for 2030.

The sustainability statement of Ishizue Holdings B.V. is published every March with the annual report. The 2030 horizon on this page is three areas the companies already work in: energy, training and materials.

40 rooftop sites · 38 MW · 40 technicians trained a year

Three areas for 2030

01 — 2030

(Energy) Plant rooms, rooftops and storage

The 2030 energy area is the work of two companies already in the group. Verda Facilities joined in 2009, is based in Utrecht, and employs 552 people in building services and maintenance. The daily scene is a technician servicing a ventilation unit in a plant room, with a colleague beside them. Ishizue Renewables joined in 2021, is based in Aarhus, and employs 120 people in rooftop solar and storage for industrial sites. A notice on 1 July 2026 recorded the 40th rooftop. Capacity across those sites is 38 MW. The panels sit on warehouse roofs the customers already use, and storage sits in the same sector line. The two companies keep their own names, bases and local management. This page states the companies, the sites and the megawatts. The year's fuller energy account is the sustainability statement published every March with the annual report.

02 — 2030

(Training) Forty technicians a year

The 2030 training area is counted in people, and the number the group publishes is Verda's. Verda Facilities trains 40 technicians a year. An instructor works with apprentices at a bench, wiring a control panel, which is the scale of the teaching. The company employs 552 people in Utrecht, in building services and maintenance, so the apprentices enter a workforce that already looks after other people's buildings. The story the group tells is titled "Apprentices first: how Verda trains 40 technicians a year." Forty is the number trained each year. Verda joined in 2009 and has kept its name and its Utrecht management. The apprentices are part of a group of 2,860 colleagues across six companies and nine countries. The sustainability statement each March carries the training account beside the annual report, in the same voluntary publication the board has made its habit.

03 — 2030

(Materials) Stone, aggregates and what is used again

The 2030 materials area sits with the oldest company. Ishizue Materials is the trade Kenzo Ishizue and Anneke de Vries began in 1962: stone and aggregates on the Maas in Rotterdam. The sector today is stone, aggregates and recycled building materials, and 640 people work in it. Recycled material is already in the description of the company, so reuse is part of the same line as the original yard. Stacked slabs and a worker checking the day's quantities are the ordinary picture of the place. The name Ishizue means foundation stone. The company has kept that name, its Rotterdam base and its local management. How a given year went, in volumes and in the way material was used again, is written in the sustainability statement published every March, with the annual report, from the head office at Maaskade 41.

A statement every March

The sustainability statement is published every March with the annual report. On 27 March 2026 the group published the annual report for 2025 and the sustainability statement together. The interim report for the first half of 2026 followed on 28 August 2026. The next annual report, for 2026, is due on 26 March 2027. Publication is voluntary: Ishizue Holdings B.V. is privately held, the Ishizue Foundation owns the majority, and the employee share plan has run since 2003. The statement covers the group of six companies and 2,860 colleagues in nine countries. Investor questions about it go to Sofia Marchetti, the CFO, at ir@ishizue-holdings.example, with a reply within two business days. A company outside the group that wants help gathering data, drafting a statement and speaking with its auditor can use the shared service priced at €9,800 a year. That fee is published, exclusive of VAT at 21 percent.

For owners

pages.title: For owners
pages.content:
When you are ready
to pass it on.

(First conversation) free and confidential.

When an owner is ready to pass a company on, Ishizue Holdings B.V. begins with a free and confidential conversation. Arjun Mehta, Head of Investments, is the person who takes it.

The companies the group will consider

Ishizue Holdings B.V. talks to owners who want continuity for a company in Northern or Western Europe. The company has been profitable for at least five years. Revenue is from €10 million to €80 million. The workforce is from 50 to 600 employees. All of those conditions sit together. The aim of the owner is that the business carry on, with its name and its people recognisable after the change. The group that would own it is six companies and 2,860 colleagues in nine countries, majority-owned by the Ishizue Foundation, with an employee share plan since 2003, privately held, reporting voluntarily. The holding office is at Maaskade 41 in Rotterdam, 58 people. Arjun Mehta, Head of Investments, takes the first approach. A business outside these bounds is outside the conversations he opens. The euro is the currency of every figure on this page.

  • Profitable for at least five years
  • Revenue of €10–80 million
  • 50 to 600 employees
  • Based in Northern or Western Europe
  • An owner who wants continuity

Five stages, in this order

The path has five stages, in this order, with the times the group actually uses.

  1. (First conversation) is free and confidential.
  2. (Business review) takes about six weeks.
  3. (Offer and terms) means one written offer.
  4. (Signing and closing) typically takes ten to fourteen weeks from the first conversation.
  5. (First 100 days) keeps the name, the management and the sites.

There is no second, competing offer from the group hiding behind the first. The weeks are counted from that opening conversation, so an owner can see the span before agreeing to start. Local management staying in place is the point of the last stage, and it matches how Northquay, Lindholm, Verda and Calder still use the names they brought. A conversation that stops after the first meeting has cost nothing. Arjun Mehta is the person who writes back.

Joined 1994

(Keep the name) Lindholm Precision since 1994

Lindholm Precision is the long example of the last stage. The company joined in 1994, is based in Gothenburg, and employs 310 people in machined components. The name on the door is still Lindholm. Management is still local. The sites are still in Gothenburg. A technician measuring a machined part with calipers beside a CNC machine is the work the company came in with, and it is the work it still does. Lindholm was the third company to join, after Ishizue Materials in 1962 and Northquay Logistics in 1978, and it was already inside the group when Ishizue Holdings B.V. was formed in 2003. The story the group publishes under the title "Keeping the name on the door: Lindholm's succession" is this fact at full length. Owners who want to read an outcome, years on, can start there.

A review, if a sale is not the question

Some owners want a written view of their options and do not want a new majority owner. That is a different piece of work, on the shared-services list. The owner succession review covers ownership options, a timetable and a written summary. The fee is €3,500, one-off, exclusive of VAT at 21 percent, and the first meeting is free. Tomasz Wrona, Head of Shared Services, is the contact for that review. A conversation about joining Ishizue stays with Arjun Mehta, and it stays free and confidential at the first step. The two paths are easy to tell apart. One ends, if both sides agree, with the Foundation as majority owner and the name, management and sites kept. The other ends with a document the current owner uses. Neither path begins with a fee on the first meeting.

How to reach Arjun Mehta

Arjun Mehta is Head of Investments at Ishizue Holdings B.V. A first conversation can start by post to Maaskade 41, 3071 NE Rotterdam, the Netherlands, by telephone to +31 10 555 0141, or by email to contact@ishizue-holdings.example, asking for him. Reception is open Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 17:30 CET. Visits are by appointment on Tuesday and Thursday. He will want to know that the company has been profitable for at least five years, that revenue sits between €10 million and €80 million, that the workforce is between 50 and 600, and that the business is in Northern or Western Europe. He will want to know that the owner is looking for continuity. Investor questions about the group itself go to Sofia Marchetti at ir@ishizue-holdings.example. The investments conversation and the investor-relations mailbox are different doors in the same building.

Shared services

pages.title: Shared services
pages.content:
Our back office,
at fixed fees.

(Fixed fees) published here.

The back office of Ishizue Holdings B.V. is open to independent companies of 20 to 300 people, at the fees published here. Tomasz Wrona, Head of Shared Services, is the contact.

(Fixed fees) Who the back office is for

Shared services are the back office of Ishizue Holdings B.V., published so that independent companies can use the same lines the group uses. The companies it is built for employ between 20 and 300 people. Fees are in euros, exclusive of VAT at 21 percent, and the six lines below are the price list. Tomasz Wrona, Head of Shared Services, is the named contact. The holding office that stands behind the work is at Maaskade 41 in Rotterdam, 58 people within a group of 2,860. An independent company buying a line does not become one of the six operating companies, and it does not pass its shares to the Ishizue Foundation. It buys a defined service at a defined fee. The first call is free. Inside the group, the same back office is how a small centre supports six trades without each company building a second copy of payroll or the monthly close.

The price list

Fees are in euros and exclusive of VAT at 21 percent.

What is not included

Each fee covers the inclusions named beside it. Payroll and HR administration means payslips, filings, leave records and one named contact. Bookkeeping and monthly close means the ledger, VAT returns and a monthly report by day 8. The treasury and insurance review means cash, banking, cover and a renewal plan, delivered once. Compliance and ethics training means the annual online course and the live session, charged per seat. Sustainability reporting support means data collection, a statement draft and auditor liaison for the year. The owner succession review means ownership options, a timetable and a written summary. Work that is not described in those lines sits outside the published fee and is agreed before anyone starts. VAT at 21 percent is added to every fee. The free first meeting applies to the succession review. The free first call applies to starting a conversation with Tomasz Wrona. A sale of a company is a different path.

How to start, and how to stop

The first call is free. Notice to end a service is 30 days. There is no minimum term beyond three months. Those three terms apply to the published list, and they are the whole of the engagement rules this page adds to the fees. To start, write to Tomasz Wrona, Head of Shared Services, at Ishizue Holdings B.V., Maaskade 41, 3071 NE Rotterdam, the Netherlands, or email contact@ishizue-holdings.example, or call +31 10 555 0141. Reception is open Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 17:30 CET, and visits are by appointment on Tuesday and Thursday. On the first call it is enough to say how many people the company employs, within the 20 to 300 the service is built for, and which line is needed. An owner who wants to talk about joining the group, rather than buying a service, should ask for Arjun Mehta instead. Investor mail goes to ir@ishizue-holdings.example.

posts.title: Keeping the name on the door: Lindholm's succession
posts.excerpt: Lindholm Precision joined Ishizue Holdings in 1994, and the Gothenburg workshop still machines components under the name it brought.
posts.content:
Lindholm Precision joined Ishizue Holdings B.V. in 1994. The company is based in Gothenburg, in Sweden, and 310 people there machine metal components. The name on the door is still Lindholm. This is the fact the story is for, and it is the fact an owner is usually asking about: after the shareholder changes, what stays.

The group already had a shape before Lindholm arrived. In 1962 Kenzo Ishizue and Anneke de Vries started a stone and aggregates trade on the Maas in Rotterdam. They called it ishizue, a word for the foundation stone. That trade continues as Ishizue Materials, still in Rotterdam, with 640 people in stone, aggregates and recycled building materials. In 1978 Northquay Logistics joined from Antwerp. Its own story opens with two trucks and a depot, and the company now employs 920 people in warehousing and regional freight. In 1987 the head office moved to Maaskade 41, 3071 NE Rotterdam, where it remains, with 58 people of the holding office. Lindholm was the next decision. It was a precision workshop, in another country, with another trade.

The work in Gothenburg is specific. A technician measures a machined part with calipers beside a CNC machine. The component is the product. The sector line the group publishes is short, machined components, and the company has stayed inside it. Local managers run the workshop. The sites are still in Gothenburg. When Ishizue talks about patient ownership, local management and keeping the name, Lindholm is the company it can attach to a year. Joined in 1994. Still Lindholm. Still machining.

The companies that joined later were left as themselves, which is the same idea carried forward. Verda Facilities joined in 2009, based in Utrecht, with 552 people in building services and maintenance, and it trains 40 technicians a year. Calder Food Partners joined in 2016, based in Hamburg, with 260 people in food ingredient distribution. Ishizue Renewables joined in 2021, based in Aarhus, with 120 people in rooftop solar and storage for industrial sites. By the notice of 1 July 2026, Renewables had completed 40 rooftop sites, together 38 MW. Add the holding office and the group counts 2,860 colleagues in nine countries: the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Denmark, Sweden, Poland, France, Spain and Ireland. Six companies, one owner. The owner is Ishizue Holdings B.V. The majority of the shares sits with the Ishizue Foundation.

In 2003 that holding company took its present form. The Foundation's majority and the employee share plan both date from that year. Lindholm was already inside the group, so the plan has been part of the life of the workshop since the plan existed. The group is privately held and publishes its reports by choice. The annual report comes every March, with the sustainability statement. On 27 March 2026 the annual report for 2025 and the sustainability statement were published. On 21 May 2026 the annual general meeting adopted all resolutions. On 28 August 2026 the interim report for the first half of 2026 was published. Through that paperwork, the door in Gothenburg still reads Lindholm Precision. An independent chair, Grace Abernethy, leads a board of seven members, four of them independent. Daniel Okoro is Group CEO. The workshop does not take its instructions from a renamed brand.

An owner reading for a present decision can set that history beside the process used now. The first conversation is free and confidential. Arjun Mehta, Head of Investments, takes it. A business review takes about six weeks. There is one written offer. Signing and closing typically take ten to fourteen weeks from the first conversation. The first 100 days keep the name, the management and the sites. The companies the group will consider have been profitable for at least five years, with revenue from €10 million to €80 million, and with 50 to 600 employees, in Northern or Western Europe. The owner wants continuity. Those bounds are the whole of the filter. Lindholm shows the outcome the last stage names, seen at a distance of years: the name, the managers and the Gothenburg sites still in place.

There is a second path for an owner who wants the thinking and wants to remain the owner. The owner succession review is a shared service. It covers ownership options, a timetable and a written summary. The fee is €3,500, one-off, exclusive of VAT at 21 percent, and the first meeting is free. Tomasz Wrona, Head of Shared Services, is the contact for that fee. A conversation about joining the group stays with Arjun Mehta, and the first conversation on that path is free. The two are different pieces of work. One can end with the Foundation as majority owner. The other ends with a written summary the current owner keeps. Publishing the fee is of a piece with the rest of the back office, which independent companies of 20 to 300 people can use at the rates on the shared-services list, beginning at €38 per employee per month for payroll and HR administration.

The founders' word means foundation stone, and the stone trade is still Ishizue Materials, on the Maas, in Rotterdam. Lindholm is a later company, in Sweden, in a different trade, kept recognisable to the people who work there. That is what the group means by laying a foundation once and building on it for decades. Anyone who wants to talk can write to Maaskade 41, call +31 10 555 0141, or use the mailbox that fits. General mail is contact@ishizue-holdings.example. Investor mail is ir@ishizue-holdings.example, for Sofia Marchetti, the CFO, and that mailbox replies within two business days. Press mail is press@ishizue-holdings.example, on the same reply time. Reception is open Monday to Friday, from 08:30 to 17:30 CET. Visits are by appointment on Tuesday and Thursday. The first conversation about a company, if the bounds above are met, costs nothing and is confidential.
